subject: Post-discovery: JSON schema / tool-calling plan for FinLytics eval
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@finlytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: J. Ortega <ops@finlytics.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: discovery earlier today — validation & structured output

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the call this morning — useful discussion. A couple quick clarifications so we can triage internally before the eval: 

- We want model recommendations specifically for structured extraction from investor decks (table-like output + nested JSON fields). Latency target is 150-250ms p50 for short prompts; QPS ~10.
- We will likely need RPC-style function/tool calling: prefer the model output to call an internal extractor if data matches X schema, otherwise return structured JSON.
- Security: we need an initial checklist for JSON schema validation and what happens on schema mismatch / retry behavior.

Attaching a sample schema and a small prompt set. Can your team propose a concrete plan (models, schema validation approach, retries, and benchmarks) and an estimated timeline for a 2-week eval?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Park
Product Lead, FinLytics

--- Attachment: finlytics_prompt_set_v1.txt (text/plain, 12 KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@finlytics.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: discovery earlier today — validation & structured output

Sarah — great to connect, and thanks for sending the sample schema + prompts. Below is a concise eval proposal and next steps for a 2-week pilot we can kick off next Monday. I kept the ask items and owners explicit so we can move quickly.

Proposal (high level)
- Recommended models: start with Open-7B-v2-quant (low-latency baseline), and Open-13B-pt-q3 (higher-quality fallback). Both are available in our hosted catalog and support function/tool calling + JSON schema enforcement via Redwood's structured output hooks.
- Validation approach: runtime JSON schema validation layer in the Redwood agent that runs post-generation. On schema mismatch, we return a structured error object and trigger a deterministic retry with the same model but alternative decoding (greedy -> temp 0.2 sampling) for up to 2 retries. If still failing, fall back to the 13B variant or routed rule to dedicated capacity for deterministic decoding.
- Retries & backoff: immediate retry for first failure (different decoding), second retry with model fallback. No exponential backoff for single-request pipelines; for bulk async extraction we recommend linear backoff and queueing.
- Benchmarks: we will run your prompt set against both models and measure schema pass-rate, schema-correct token ratio, latency p50/p95, and token cost. I attached our baseline CSV template for results.

Attachments we will provide
- Redwood eval harness config (driver + prompt bindings)
- Benchmarks CSV (we will populate) — see link below

Timeline (2-week pilot)
- Day 0 (Mon): ingest sample schema & prompt set, confirm endpoints and credentials (FinLytics ops).
- Day 1–3: run baseline pass with Open-7B-v2-quant; collect schema pass-rate and latency.
- Day 4–7: run targeted retries/fallbacks and rule tuning; run Open-13B-pt-q3 on failure cases.
- Day 8–10: aggregate results, identify regression concerns, propose quality guardrails (prompt templates, canonicalization utilities).
- Day 11–14: produce final report + recommended production settings (batching, caching, qparams).

Immediate asks from FinLytics (action items)
1) Confirm we can use the sample schema as the canonical eval schema or send a revised one (owner: Sarah).
2) Provide a test API key or allow Redwood a short-lived eval token for runnables (owner: J. Ortega).
3) Any redlines on latency targets (owner: Sarah).

Next steps
- Camila will build the eval harness and Marcus will instrument the JSON validation + retry flow. Naomi will own contract/PO if you need a reserved seat for Dedicated testing.

Links
- Preliminary benchmark profile: https://benchmarks.redwood/models/open-7b-v2-profile
- Shared drive (we will populate): https://drive.redwood/company/finlytics/eval-plan

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync to review the plan with your ops team tomorrow at noon PST — does that work?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@finlytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: J. Ortega <ops@finlytics.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: discovery earlier today — validation & structured output

Evelyn — thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifying questions before we confirm the schedule: 

1) On schema mismatch you described returning a structured error object — can you paste an example payload? We want to ensure our downstream services can parse the error deterministically.
2) For retries: is the retry happening client-side (we re-call) or server-side (Redwood will re-emit and only return final result)? Prefer server-side but want to understand visibility for telemetry.
3) Any guidance on whether the function/tool calling should be synchronous (single request/response) vs. async job for batches? We will have some large deck ingestion jobs alongside low-latency inline extraction.

Attached a slightly updated schema that adds a required field `source_page` — happy to use that as the canonical schema if it helps.

Thanks — Sarah

--- Attachment: finlytics_sample_schema_v2.json (application/json, 8 KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: FinLytics eval — next steps and owners (schema v2 intake)

Team — looping you in on Sarah's updated schema (they added `source_page`) and her questions about implementation. Action items below; please reply with ETA by EOD.

Action items
- Camila: update the eval harness to ingest finlytics_sample_schema_v2.json and bind it as the canonical validation schema. Deliverable: harness config + example run (ETA: 2026-11-11T10:00-08:00).
- Marcus: implement the server-side retry flow inside the Redwood agent: first retry = change decoding to greedy (temp=0.0), second retry = route to fallback model (Open-13B-pt-q3). Return a deterministic error object if both retries fail. Add telemetry tags: schema_pass(boolean), retries_used(int), fallback_triggered(boolean). (ETA: 2026-11-12).
- Naomi: prep PO language for a 2-week eval; include optional Dedicated trial if FinLytics wants guaranteed latency. (ETA: 2026-11-11).
- Rafael: own the customer sync tomorrow at noon PST — confirm internal participants and finalize calendar invite.

Example error payload (send back to FinLytics on mismatch):
{
  "status": "error",
  "reason": "schema_mismatch",
  "errors": ["missing field: investor_count", "type_mismatch: term_sheet -> expected array"]
}

Notes on retry visibility: we will perform retries server-side and return only the final response to the client by default. For telemetry and debugging we will surface the intermediate attempts in the Console and via the eval harness logs (request_id -> attempt_n). We should prepare a short example doc for Sarah showing the Console traces.

Sync plan: Rafael, please confirm that Sarah & J. Ortega can join the 11/11 12:00 PST review. Naomi, please have PO language ready so we can execute the eval when they sign off.

Thanks — small, fast steps. Happy to pair with Marcus for the telemetry schema if helpful.

Evelyn
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
